If this story is rooted in historical events and the work of a well-known human rights activist, why did the film reportedly face years of hurdles before reaching audiences? And after finally becoming available on Zee5, why was it reportedly taken dowr again within just two days?
Was this purely due to legal or licensing reasons, or were there other concerns? If so, why hasn’t there been a clear public explanation from the government, the censor board, or the platform?
If a film presents a particular interpretation of historical events, shouldn’t people be allowed to watch it, examine the evidence, and form their own conclusions instead of having that opportunity limited?
History should be debated, questioned, and understood, not left surrounded by speculation.
If you managed to watch Sutlej before it was removed, what did you think? Did it help you better understand the events surrounding 1995 in Punjab? Was it balanced, compelling, or did it raise more questions? Share your views respectfully so others can understand why this film has generated so much discussion.
A transparent explanation would do more to build public trust than silence ever could.
